summary: The selected dual-wield acid-breath mismatch was caused by the missing trap.c:acid_damage() helper. The full erode_obj(), grease_protect(), and acid_damage() family is now implemented in js/trap_erode_obj.js; zap.c:zhitu and zhitm plus mhitu.c:passiveum call the canonical helper, and the v42 replay now matches through step 83. Fresh C-first Zhitu, zhitm, passiveum, and greased acid-dip cases provide independent matching evidence. The armed monster-vs-monster passivemm caller is wired and source-pinned but its production entry remains blocked before passivemm at JavaScript step 132.

source.branch: acid_damage returns on a null object or acid-resistant hero inventory; grease absorbs the effect; nonblank scrolls become blank paper; other objects are passed to erode_obj with ERODE_CORRODE and EF_GREASE|EF_VERBOSE.
callers: zap.c:zhitu calls acid_damage(uwep) and acid_damage(uswapwep) under distinct weapon gates; js/zap.js now passes the canonical state.uwep and state.uswapwep slots to trap_erode_obj.js:acid_damage.
zap.c:zhitm calls acid_damage(MON_WEP(mon)); js/zap.js calls the same helper after the source rn2(6) gate.
mhitu.c:passiveum calls acid_damage(MON_WEP(mtmp)); js/mhitu.js now calls the same helper after the source rn2(6) gate.

mhitm.c:passivemm calls acid_damage(MON_WEP(magr)); js/mhitm.js now calls the helper and has source-pinned coverage, but the selected production route stops earlier in the existing armed monster-vs-monster mattackm path.
uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_acid also calls acid_damage(MON_WEP(mdef)); the existing js/uhitm.js dispatch still marks this caller unported and it is outside this task.
dependencies: trap.c:erode_obj, grease_protect, and acid_damage share the canonical js/trap_erode_obj.js implementation; acid_damage retains the source order for hero acid resistance, grease, scroll blanking, then ERODE_CORRODE.
zap.c:inventory_resistance_check is already implemented in js/zap.js.
The dual-wield production fix uses the canonical top-level state.uwep and state.uswapwep slots that correspond to C u.uwep and u.uswapwep.

evidence: The saved v42 queue selected this session at the final weapon-corrosion message. The accepted baseline at 990f9bc4c2964447a9adac4f0e54ea90728ee2cb had 83/84 screens, 3005/3005 RNG values, and 83/84 cursors; its first mismatch was step 83.

Upstream trap.c:acid_damage() (4618-4654) checks a null object, carried hero acid resistance, grease, blank-paper/mail exceptions, then erode_obj(obj, NULL, ERODE_CORRODE, EF_GREASE|EF_VERBOSE). The port preserves that order and maps carried objects to the canonical hero inventory state.

Upstream trap.c:grease_protect() (360-386) prints the source visibility-dependent message, rolls rn2(2), clears grease only on zero, and refreshes inventory only for a carried object. The port keeps this as one canonical helper shared by erode_obj() and acid_damage().

Upstream trap.c:erode_obj() (171-353) uses the source erosion tables, victim selection, inventory-resistance draw, grease guard, vulnerability and erosion-proof checks, message ordering, destruction cleanup, and return codes. The B42 changes retain the existing whole-function implementation and use it from acid_damage().

The matching fresh Zhitu dual-wield recording reaches zap.c:zhitu at step 81: the main-hand rn2(3) gate succeeds, the off-hand gate fails, and the katana corrodes. Its complete 82-step C-first recipe replay matches PRNG, screens, cursors, and animation frames.

The matching fresh zhitm recording reaches zap.c:zhitm at step 103, passes the source rn2(6) acid_damage gate, and matches the complete 104-step C-first replay. This recording does not show weapon corrosion, so it is evidence for the caller path only.

The matching fresh passiveum recording reaches mhitu.c:passiveum at step 65, including the successful rn2(6) acid_damage gate, and matches the complete 66-step C-first replay. The visible output does not establish an erode_obj effect for that call.

The matching fresh acid-dip recording reaches trap.c:grease_protect at step 61 (rn2(2)=0), reports grease protection, then dissolves the grease at step 62. Its complete 66-step C-first replay matches PRNG, screens, and cursors.

The preserved passivemm recipe records a C path through mhitm.c:passivemm: at step 135, rn2(30)=4 and rn2(6)=0 select acid_damage, followed by pick-axe corrosion at step 137. The JavaScript replay stops at step 132 with the existing UnsupportedTurnBoundaryError for an armed monster attacking another monster, before passivemm executes. Do not count that recipe or its removed nonmatching recording as runtime evidence.
